input.question: Why is naming your boat a thing but you don't see anyone doing it with their cars.
input.ground_truth: Boats have to identify themselves via radio traffic, so a name is useful. The tradition is older than that, so I'll guess it's because they needed to distinguish between ships so that they'd be able to refer to them specifically. "My husband is on the Quicksilver." There is less call for that with cars.

Boats are special because people take them on adventures on the big water, so giving them a name makes it feel like they’re part of the adventure, almost like a friend.

Now, think about your toy car. You might play with it, but it usually stays with you on the ground, not going on big trips by itself. Cars don’t go out on their own adventures in the same way boats do. So, people don’t usually give cars names like they do boats. But you *could* name your car if you want to! Some people do, especially if they really love their car.

So, naming things is a way to show you care about them and make them feel special. Boats get named a lot because they go on big journeys, but you could name anything you love!
